主要内容: 2013 marked a historic year for collector cars, with auction sales in the U.S. reaching an all-time high of $1.2 billion, a 25% increase from 2012. The average price per car sold rose 13% to $61,000, with the top-end market seeing significant spikes, particularly for vintage Ferraris, Mercedes, and Porsches. Four of the top five most expensive collector cars ever sold at auction were sold in 2013. Hagerty Insurance, the largest insurer of collectible cars, noted that the Ferrari index rose 18%, making Ferraris the most expensive category. German cars, including Porsche, Mercedes, and BMW, also saw a 33% increase. Despite the price growth, McKeel Hagerty, president of Hagerty, stated there are few signs of a bubble, citing strong supply and demand. The year was also notable for the race between a 1967 Ferrari and a 1954 Mercedes-Benz W196R to become the most expensive car ever sold at auction. The Ferrari sold for $27.5 million, just short of the Mercedes' $29.7 million. Hagerty predicted a $100 million car sale within the next three to five years, likely a Ferrari GTO. The year 2013 marked a significant milestone in the world of collector cars, becoming the most successful year ever for classic car auctions. The top five most expensive cars sold in 2013 included the 1954 Mercedes-Benz W196R, which fetched $29,700,000 at Bonhams in July 2013. The 1967 Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S NART Spyder sold for $27,500,000 at RM in August 2013. Other notable sales included the 1964 Ferrari 250 LM at $14,300,000, the 1953 Ferrari 340/375 MM Berlinetta Competizione at $12,800,000, and the 1957 Ferrari 250 GT TdF Berlinetta at $9,460,000. These sales reflect the growing interest and value of classic cars in the market, with auction prices reaching unprecedented levels in 2013.
